Psi(k) = sum of squares of the (k+1) distinct Fibonacci subwords of length k,
each interpreted as a decimal integer (leading zeros ignored).

Computed by naive brute force: build Fibonacci words S_N until the length-k
factor set stabilises at size k+1; sum squares of the integer values.

Verification:
  Psi(3) = 20302                       (worked example, exact match)
  Psi(10) mod 101001001 = 10699667     (worked example, exact match)
  |set| == k+1 held for every k = 1..30 (stabilisation fact confirmed)

Values for k=15,16,23..26 supersede an earlier run whose N bound was too small
and which therefore silently missed factors (returned too-large count->smaller
set). The tightest word length N needed for each k is tiny (N=9 suffices for
all k<=30), far below the n=40 ceiling.
